The foundation of Blake and Boky's collaborative work. This collection explores the beauty within, opening up the figure and diving into the inner structure. The driving force behind this project was to expose the inner world of the figure, one that usually isn't seen. Drawing attention to what is usually hidden became a conduit for deeper introspection. Subsequently, the engineering behind this first desire to open the figure also tied into the second desire : allowing the sculpture to be both static and in movement. Every artwork in this collection is subject to the rule of physics whereby their structure allows them to "dance" and be alive in accordance to their environment.

Re-Think Collection is dedicated to the promotion of human rights.

The ReThink Collection began to take form slowly and without a specific intention to build a series of sculpture that commented on Human Rights or the actions of authoritarian governments. (1989 Emerging Continents, commenting on the Tiananmen Square Massacre). Nor did I ever think that the issue of Women’s Rights, (which inspired the sculptural work; The Burden – Glass Ceiling) would become a source of energy to build socio-political works. Yet, The Bench, provided an opportunity to present commentary on an historic injustice and thus I designed it to be supported by two males as caryatides, facing forward holding each end of the seat while a lone female figure supported the back of the platform, facing in the opposite direction.
— Tomas Nguyen, Clara Delaunay, Idriss B.

This sculpture is a quiet reflection on our role in the degradation of our ecosystem and the challenges of the Anthropocene era. It resonates with the humanitarian crises and the shadows of war that cloud our world. Yet, it refuses to surrender to despair. The inversion challenges us to re-evaluate our approach, to question the status quo, and to consider a path toward healing.

The radiant light that emanates from the sculpture is not just symbolic; it's a promise—a promise that we possess the power to mend, to restore, and to flourish. It reminds us that even when our world seems to hang upside down, we have the ability to set it right and create a future where our dreams can indeed flourish.

In its minimalist elegance, this sculpture serves as a poignant call to awaken from our environmental apathy. It implores us to listen to the cries of a planet in peril, to acknowledge the urgency of the Anthropocene, and to take tangible steps to mitigate the destruction of our ecosystem.

Silentium Aurum abandons the formal language of
sculpture, reducing it to its essence ; material, light, and word. Gold-leafed
steel, carved with language, holds silence as its most valuable element.
Here, gold is not about opulence but reverence; silence is not emptiness
but weight. The light that escapes through each word is not mere
illumination—it is an invitation, a quiet insistence on introspection.
Not about the objects themselves but about what they stir within us. Each piece exists in the liminal space between presence and
absence, between what is spoken and what is only felt. Whispering
Skies and Restless Angels do not dictate meaning; they reflect it back,
shaped by the viewer’s own memories, desires, and truths. The unseen,
the in-between—this is where Silentium Aurum resides.
If Silentium spoke through absence, then Silentium Aurum refines that
absence into something luminous. It captures not the known, but the
fleeting—what we long for, what we remember, what we have yet to
understand. Here, silence is not void. It is precious. It is gold.
